prompt: Spending crosses 100% of a budget. What does Google do on its own?

choices.text: Stops every machine in the projects
choices.why: Budgets stop nothing. Stopping is something a subscriber would have to do.

choices.text: Sends the alerts the budget asks for
choices.why: Right. E-mail, and a Pub/Sub message if configured. Nothing is stopped.

choices.text: Unlinks the projects from billing
choices.why: Only a program the customer writes would do that.

choices.text: Charges the excess to the next month
choices.why: The excess is billed this month like the rest.

prompt: Why does the planner budget have a 100% threshold on forecasted spend as well as on actual spend?

choices.text: Google requires one of each
choices.why: Any mix is accepted; the forecast is there for the warning.

choices.text: The forecast stops spending and the actual one reports it
choices.why: Neither stops anything.

choices.text: Forecasted thresholds cost less to run
choices.why: Budgets cost nothing either way.

choices.text: The forecast warns while there is time to act
choices.why: Right. It can fire on the fifth day, weeks before the actual one.

prompt: In the plan, three thresholds came back with `spend_basis = CURRENT_SPEND` though the file named none. Why?
hint: Defaults show up in a plan.

choices.text: Actual spend is the default
choices.why: Right. Only a threshold that says `FORECASTED_SPEND` looks ahead.

choices.text: Google read the current month's spend
choices.why: A plan asked Google nothing.

choices.text: The last threshold's basis was copied to the others
choices.why: The last one says forecasted; the others came out different.

choices.text: The emulator filled it in
choices.why: The emulator is Pub/Sub only.

prompt: A burst of spending starts at 14:00. The budget's 90% threshold is crossed by it. When will the alert arrive?
hint: Costs reach the billing data with a delay.

choices.text: At 14:00, the moment the spend happens
choices.why: Billing data is not real time; budgets inherit its delay.

choices.text: At the end of the month, with the invoice
choices.why: Budgets are evaluated several times a day, not monthly.

choices.text: Hours later
choices.why: Right. A budget measures where the money was, not where it is.

choices.text: Never, because bursts are averaged away
choices.why: Nothing averages them away; they arrive late, not never.

prompt: A budget of 300 dollars has a 90% threshold. At how many dollars of spend does it fire?
What does `all_updates_rule` with a `pubsub_topic` ask Google to do?

choices.text: Create the topic if it is missing
choices.why: The topic has to exist; the rule only names it.

choices.text: Stop publishing to the topic past 100%
choices.why: Publishing goes on; past 100% is when it matters most.

choices.text: Publish the budget's state there
choices.why: Right. Several times a day, threshold or not, for a program to read.

choices.text: Send e-mail through Pub/Sub
choices.why: E-mail is separate. The topic is for programs.

prompt: In the lab, who published the three budget messages?

choices.text: The course, in Google's format
choices.why: Right. In the lab nobody else publishes; the program's decisions on them are real.

choices.text: Google's Cloud Billing, through the emulator
choices.why: Nothing of Google's publishes into the emulator.

choices.text: The Terraform budget, once planned
choices.why: A plan creates nothing, budgets included.

choices.text: The emulator, which simulates billing
choices.why: The emulator is Pub/Sub and knows no costs.

prompt: `on_budget.py` never says where Pub/Sub is. How does it reach the emulator?

choices.text: Through the `api_endpoint_overrides/pubsub` property
choices.why: That property is gcloud's; the client library ignores it.

choices.text: Through the placeholder token
choices.why: A token says who, not where.

choices.text: The emulator is the library's default
choices.why: The default is Google; the variable changes it.

choices.text: The library reads `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST`
choices.why: Right. Unset, the same file would read the real subscription.

prompt: Why does `on_budget.py` compute the share itself rather than read `alertThresholdExceeded`?

choices.text: The field is always wrong by a few cents
choices.why: It names a threshold, not an amount.

choices.text: It is absent until one is crossed
choices.why: Right. The first message had no such field, and the program still had to decide.

choices.text: The emulator strips that field
choices.why: The second and third messages carried it through the emulator.

choices.text: Python cannot read fields with capital letters
choices.why: It reads `costAmount` in the same message.

prompt: Why does the program acknowledge each message?

choices.text: So Pub/Sub does not deliver it again
choices.why: Right. An unacknowledged message comes back after its deadline.

choices.text: To tell Google's billing it was read
choices.why: The acknowledgement goes to Pub/Sub, not to billing.

choices.text: To delete the topic
choices.why: Acknowledging touches one message, not the topic.

choices.text: To raise the budget
choices.why: Nothing in a Pub/Sub acknowledgement changes a budget.

prompt: Put the path of a budget alert that acts in order.
hint: From the bill to the decision.
items: Google publishes to the budget's topic
a subscriber pulls the message and decides
trap: Putting the evaluation before the costs arrive is the slip: the budget only ever sees what the billing data already holds, which is why alerts come late.

prompt: Is there a Google Cloud setting that stops all spending at a fixed amount?
hint: Who would choose what to switch off?

choices.text: Yes, the budget's 100% threshold
choices.why: That threshold sends a message and stops nothing.

choices.text: Yes, the free trial's credit
choices.why: The credit ends; it does not cap a paid account.

choices.text: No; the customer builds one, or uses quotas
choices.why: Right. A hard cap would decide which systems to stop and which data to lose.

choices.text: Yes, an organisation policy
choices.why: Policies constrain what may be created, not what it costs.

prompt: A bug makes the planner call a paid translation API in a loop. Which cap fails only that, and leaves the rest running?
hint: The finest of the three tools.

choices.text: A budget with an automated unlink
choices.why: That stops everything in the project, not just the API.

choices.text: A lowered rate quota on that API
choices.why: Right. The loop is refused at the quota instead of billed at the price.

choices.text: A forecasted threshold at 100%
choices.why: It warns; the loop keeps calling.

choices.text: A deny policy on the project
choices.why: It would refuse the API to everybody, the working code too.

prompt: A new project is linked to the company's billing account next week. The planner budget lists its three projects by name. What catches the new project's spending?
hint: A budget sees only what its filter names.

choices.text: The planner budget, as it covers the account
choices.why: It names three projects; the new one is outside its filter.

choices.text: The new project's default budget
choices.why: Projects get no budget by default.

choices.text: The project's quotas
choices.why: Quotas limit use; they report no spending to anybody.

choices.text: A budget on the whole account
choices.why: Right. With no project filter, it sees every project, the new ones included.

prompt: Match each way of limiting spending to what it costs when it bites.

pairs.left: a budget with an automated unlink
pairs.right: everything stops; data may be deleted

pairs.left: a sandbox project with a small budget

prompt: The planner team wants production never to be switched off by a cost rule, and the sandbox never to surprise them. Which arrangement fits both?

choices.text: An automated unlink on both
choices.why: That switches production off, which the team ruled out.

choices.text: One budget on both, at the sandbox's amount
choices.why: Production's spend would cross it on the first day.

choices.text: No budgets, and quotas set to zero
choices.why: Zero quotas run nothing, production included.

choices.text: A person for one, an unlink for the other
choices.why: Right. Production keeps running and somebody decides; the sandbox can lose everything.
